title: Best Encrypted Messaging Apps Compared
metaDescription: Signal, WhatsApp, Telegram, Element and Threema compared on encryption, metadata, open source, sign-up and disappearing messages, on one published rubric.
intro: Choosing the right encrypted messaging app is crucial for protecting your private conversations. With governments and hackers increasingly targeting digital communications, end-to-end encryption has become essential for everyone from activists to everyday users.

products.name: Signal
products.tagline: End-to-end encrypted messaging with disappearing messages
pros: Open source; its encryption protocol has been independently analysed
Disappearing messages for any chat, with an optional default timer
Phone number hidden from others by default; usernames available
cons: Smaller user base than mainstream apps

products.name: WhatsApp
products.tagline: Meta's messaging app, end-to-end encrypted by default
cons: Cloud backups aren't end-to-end encrypted unless you turn that on
Shares your phone number with people you chat with (optional usernames are still rolling out)

products.name: Telegram
products.tagline: Cloud messaging app with optional end-to-end encrypted Secret Chats
pros: Large group chats up to 200,000 members
cons: Secret chats aren't available in Telegram Desktop or on the web
Uses its own MTProto encryption protocol instead of the Signal Protocol

products.name: Element (Matrix)
pros: Rich text formatting and file sharing
cons: Can be complex for non-technical users

products.name: Threema
products.tagline: Swiss messaging app that needs no phone number
products.pricing: One-time purchase (CHF 6 from Threema; store prices vary by country)
pros: No phone number or email required
cons: Paid app with small user base
Limited feature set compared to free alternatives

verdict.summary: On these six criteria Element (Matrix) and Signal tie for the top score; Element is listed first only because ties are ordered alphabetically. Signal encrypts everything by default, keeps very little metadata and is open source, but needs a phone number to sign up. Element is open source and decentralized and needs no phone number, but it has no disappearing-messages timer and takes more effort to learn. Threema comes next: it needs no phone number or email, but it is a paid app and its server code is closed. Telegram and WhatsApp score lowest: Telegram encrypts end to end only in Secret Chats, and WhatsApp encrypts chats by default but is closed source and collects more metadata.

pro_tips: If you use a messaging app's web version, keep the browser up to date and sign out when you're done, especially on shared computers.
Enable disappearing messages even on encrypted apps to minimize data stored on devices in case of physical compromise.
Verify contact identity through in-person key exchange or secondary channels before sharing sensitive information.
Turn off cloud backups or make sure they're end-to-end encrypted; WhatsApp's backups are end-to-end encrypted only if you turn that on.
Consider using different messaging apps for different purposes - Signal for sensitive communications, others for casual chats.

faqs.question: What does end-to-end encryption actually mean?
faqs.answer: End-to-end encryption means your messages are scrambled on your device and can only be unscrambled on the recipient's device. Even the messaging service provider cannot read your messages, as they don't have the decryption keys.

faqs.question: Is WhatsApp really secure if it's owned by Meta?
faqs.answer: WhatsApp uses strong end-to-end encryption for message content, but Meta collects extensive metadata about your communications patterns, contacts, and usage habits. Your message content is secure, but your privacy isn't fully protected.

faqs.question: Why isn't Telegram encrypted by default?
faqs.answer: Telegram prioritizes features like cloud synchronization and large groups over default encryption. Their regular chats use client-server encryption, allowing messages to sync across devices but making them accessible to Telegram's servers.

faqs.question: Can law enforcement access my encrypted messages?
faqs.answer: With proper end-to-end encryption, law enforcement cannot access message content from the service provider. However, they might obtain messages from unlocked devices, compel you to unlock devices, or use other surveillance methods.

faqs.question: Should I trust apps that aren't open-source?
faqs.answer: Open-source apps allow independent security audits and verification of encryption claims. While some closed-source apps may be secure, you must trust the company's claims without being able to verify them independently.

faqs.question: How do I convince friends and family to switch to more secure messaging?
faqs.answer: Start by explaining privacy benefits in simple terms, offer to help with setup, and suggest using secure apps for specific conversations rather than completely replacing their current apps. Lead by example and be patient with the transition.
